open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: The required categories are the closed set that canonical grammar defines
open_points.question: What is the exact closed set of required category names?
options: Treat the nine categories shown in the Security review as the complete set
Use a separately defined canonical set that may differ from the nine shown
open_points.default_guess: Treat the nine categories shown as the complete required set.

witness.initial: A review record contains exactly the nine categories printed in A21.
events: The author submits the record to design_lint --state 2.
design_lint compares its categories with the required set.
outcomes: The record passes because the printed nine categories define the closed set.
The record fails because an externally defined canonical set contains another required category.
witness.observer: The author running the State 2 gate

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: The record follows the Workbench's canonical security-review grammar
open_points.question: What is the complete syntax and field schema of the review record that design_lint must parse?
options: Parse the displayed Markdown bullets and their semicolon-separated fields
Require a separate structured record with fields such as category, outcome, references, rationale and affected
open_points.default_guess: Parse the displayed Security review bullets as the canonical record.

witness.initial: A21 contains only the displayed Markdown Security review section.
events: The linter searches for one complete review record.
outcomes: The linter recognizes the Markdown bullets as the record and validates them.
The linter reports that no canonical structured record exists.
witness.observer: The author and the State 3 gate

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: a missing, repeated or unknown category fails the gate
open_points.question: How must the formal invariant reject an additional unknown category when all required categories still have one outcome?
options: Unknown categories independently make the gate fail, as the normative rule and required test state
Apply the stated biconditional literally; an extra category does not falsify every_required_category_has_one_outcome
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit no_unknown_categories condition to the gate.

witness.initial: One record contains every required category exactly once, no UNRESOLVED outcome, valid references, and one extra category named future_risk.
events: The author submits the record to the State 2 gate.
The gate evaluates both the normative rule and state2_security_gate_pass.
outcomes: The normative rule and required test reject the record because future_risk is unknown.
The formal biconditional passes because every required category has one outcome, every reference resolves, every APPLICABLE category has an accepted decision, and there is no UNRESOLVED outcome.
witness.observer: The author and any implementation of design_lint

open_points.subject: context
open_points.question: Must the gate reject a NOT_APPLICABLE category whose rationale is absent or empty, despite the formal gate invariant having no rationale condition?
options: Reject it because a non-empty rationale is part of the outcome definition
Accept it when the four formal invariant terms hold
open_points.default_guess: Reject it and add an explicit non-empty-rationale condition to the invariant.

witness.initial: Every required category appears once; browser_boundary is NOT_APPLICABLE with an empty rationale; all other categories are valid and none is UNRESOLVED.
events: The author submits the record to design_lint --state 2.
The gate evaluates the outcome definition and the formal biconditional.
outcomes: The outcome definition rejects browser_boundary because its rationale is not non-empty.
The formal biconditional passes because category presence, references, APPLICABLE decisions and no_UNRESOLVED all hold.
witness.observer: The author and the State 3 gate

open_points.subject: context
open_points.question: Which indexed fact determines that an accepted decision belongs to States 0–2?
options: Use explicit state metadata stored on each design-index item
Infer the state from the source document or section containing the decision
Infer eligibility from the A-number or accept every indexed item of kind decision
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit state metadata on the indexed item and accept only state numbers 0, 1 or 2.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE category references key A30, whose indexed item has kind decision but was authored in State 3; the supplied definition of an accepted decision exposes only kind decision.
events: The linter resolves A30 in the design index.
The linter tests whether the APPLICABLE category has an accepted decision of States 0–2.
outcomes: The record fails because A30's source location or metadata identifies State 3.
The record passes because every indexed item of kind decision is treated as an accepted decision and no stated index field identifies its state.
witness.observer: The author waiting to enter State 3

open_points.subject: context
open_points.question: What indexed kind or other test identifies a reference target as an open question?
options: Require an indexed item with an explicitly defined open-question kind
Treat any unresolved prose section or model Open questions entry as an open question
Require only that the reference resolve, because UNRESOLVED fails the gate regardless
open_points.default_guess: Require a distinct indexed open-question kind, and reject an UNRESOLVED record whose reference does not name one.

witness.initial: A category has outcome UNRESOLVED and references an indexed prose item that describes undecided work but has no stated open-question kind.
events: The linter validates the UNRESOLVED outcome before failing the gate.
outcomes: The record is structurally valid but gate-blocking because the prose item counts as an open question.
The record is malformed because only a specifically typed open-question item may be referenced.
witness.observer: The review author diagnosing why State 3 is blocked

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: affected is review evidence for the reader
open_points.question: Is affected a required field, when must it be non-empty, and does its absence make the record malformed even though the gate does not check coverage?
options: Require non-empty affected evidence for every APPLICABLE category and allow it to be absent for NOT_APPLICABLE
Require affected on every category
Treat affected as optional reader-only prose
open_points.default_guess: Require non-empty affected evidence for APPLICABLE categories and permit its absence for NOT_APPLICABLE categories.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE category has valid accepted-decision references but omits affected.
events: The author submits the otherwise complete record.
The linter checks canonical grammar and then the stated gate invariant.
outcomes: The record is rejected because affected is a required evidence field.
The record passes because coverage is review judgement and the gate checks the record, not that coverage.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: design_lint --state 2 accepts exactly one complete review record
open_points.question: Does the gate reject a case containing two individually complete review records, and how are record boundaries identified?
options: Require exactly one record per case and reject zero or multiple records
Validate the latest complete record and ignore earlier records
Merge category entries across all review sections into one record
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one syntactically delimited review record and reject zero or multiple records.

witness.initial: The case contains two complete Security review sections, each with every required category and valid outcomes.
outcomes: The gate rejects the case because it requires exactly one record.
The gate accepts the latest record or merges both because neither record boundaries nor multiple-record behavior are defined.
witness.observer: The author and the State 3 gate
